alt.en: Part of a printed advertisement page. A boxed heading reads "Let Me Call You Sweetheart, By Leo Friedman and Beth Slater Whitson", above a paragraph calling it "the new song sensation by the writers of 'Meet Me To-Night in Dreamland'". Below is the song's chorus for voice and piano, "Let me call you 'Sweetheart' I'm in love with you", and at the foot: "Copyright MCMX by Leo Friedman, Chicago. British Copyright Secured. Copyright Assigned Dec. 13, 1910 to Harold Rossiter Music Co., Chicago."
alt.es: Parte de una página impresa de publicidad. Un encabezado enmarcado dice "Let Me Call You Sweetheart, By Leo Friedman and Beth Slater Whitson", sobre un párrafo que la llama "the new song sensation by the writers of 'Meet Me To-Night in Dreamland'". Debajo está el estribillo de la canción para voz y piano, "Let me call you 'Sweetheart' I'm in love with you", y al pie: "Copyright MCMX by Leo Friedman, Chicago. British Copyright Secured. Copyright Assigned Dec. 13, 1910 to Harold Rossiter Music Co., Chicago."

caption.en: A Harold Rossiter Music Company advertisement of 1911, on the back cover of another of its songs, prints the chorus over the notice that Friedman's copyright was assigned to Rossiter on 13 December 1910.
caption.es: Un anuncio de la Harold Rossiter Music Company de 1911, en la contraportada de otra de sus canciones, imprime el estribillo sobre el aviso de que el copyright de Friedman se cedió a Rossiter el 13 de diciembre de 1910.

source: Shelton Brooks, There'll Come a Time (Chicago: Harold Rossiter Music Co., copyright 1911), back cover, advertisement for Let Me Call You Sweetheart (detail)

alt.en: A printed paragraph under the heading "Read This---It's Interesting", with a decorated capital T: "There seems to be some sort of magic charm about the song 'LET ME CALL YOU SWEETHEART,' ... 'Let Me Call You Sweetheart' is the first and only song that has ever 'come back' into a second wave of popularity. It was one of the big song hits of 1911 and is now once again the biggest selling popular song on the market."

It was one of the big song hits of 1911 and is now once again the biggest selling popular song on the market."

caption.en: Rossiter's advertising of 1925, inside the cover of a later printing: the song is "the first and only song that has ever 'come back'", a hit of 1911 and once again the biggest seller on the market.

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "Let Me Call You Sweetheart (I'm in Love with You.)", "Music by Leo Friedman and Words by Beth Slater Whitson", "Writers of 'Meet Me To-Night in Dreamland'", with a boxed line "Ask Your Dealer for a Player-Roll or Phonograph Record of This Piece". It is marked "Moderato", for voice and piano in 3/4 with two flats, with two verses under the notes: "I am dream-ing Dear of you Day by day" and "Long-ing for you all the while More and more". At the foot: "Copyright MCMX, by Harold Rossiter Music Co. Chicago, Ill. International Copyright Secured" and "NOTE: This song is also published for Male and Mixed Quartette, and also for Band and Orchestra."
alt.es: Una página impresa de música con el encabezado "Let Me Call You Sweetheart (I'm in Love with You.)", "Music by Leo Friedman and Words by Beth Slater Whitson", "Writers of 'Meet Me To-Night in Dreamland'", y un recuadro que dice "Ask Your Dealer for a Player-Roll or Phonograph Record of This Piece". Está marcada "Moderato", para voz y piano en 3/4 con dos bemoles, con dos estrofas bajo las notas: "I am dream-ing Dear of you Day by day" y "Long-ing for you all the while More and more". Al pie: "Copyright MCMX, by Harold Rossiter Music Co. Chicago, Ill. International Copyright Secured" y "NOTE: This song is also published for Male and Mixed Quartette, and also for Band and Orchestra."

caption.en: The first page of music in a later Rossiter printing, "The New Edition": the verse, Moderato in B-flat and 3/4, both verses on one tune, and a note that the song was also sold for male and mixed quartet, band and orchestra.
caption.es: La primera página de música de una impresión posterior de Rossiter, "The New Edition": la estrofa, Moderato en Si bemol y en 3/4, las dos estrofas sobre la misma melodía y una nota que dice que la canción se vendía también para cuarteto masculino y mixto, banda y orquesta.
